newsitem.title: UK: Blair most popular British prime minister ever.
newsitem.headline: Blair most popular British prime minister ever.

text.p: Tony Blair is Britain's most popular prime minister since polling began, achieving an approval rating of 82 percent five weeks after his Labour Party won a landslide election victory, a poll showed.
The Gallup Poll in Friday's Daily Telegraph also showed more people claimed to have voted Labour in the May 1 election -- 53 percent -- than actually did -- 44 percent.
A change of government after 18 years of Conservative rule has triggered a mood of optimism in Britain and Labour has introduced, or signalled, a number of far-reaching reforms.
Fifty one percent of those polled said the government's performance had been good. Another 13 percent viewed it as "excellent".
Blair's rating eclipses the record held by Conservative premier Harold Macmillan who recorded 79 percent in a Gallup poll in May 1960.
But Blair should not get too carried away by this tidal wave of voter support as his predecessor John Major can vouch for the fickleness of poll ratings.
In February 1991, boosted by his performance during the Gulf War and three months after he took over as prime minister, Major earned the approval of 74 percent of the electorate.
This eclipsed the 53 percent rating of his predecessor, Margaret Thatcher, achieved in the 1982 Falklands War.

But by July 1993, Major's rating had fallen to the lowest ever, just 14 percent, after his Conservative party was split open by disagreements over Europe and sterling's ignominious withdrawal from the European exchange rate mechanism.
